pf.license.blocks going live: A CPA firm with no active CPA license on file in that state stays offline there for CPA work. A CPA whose license isn't active is never shown as 'CPA' and isn't offered for CPA-only work.
pf.license.renewals: Checked on each renewal date from the state form; a lapsed license pauses that person's CPA-only bookings, and Sam is told.
pf.license.insurance: Professional liability insurance on file where the state's rules require it; the amount comes from the state form.

pf.money.before: Flow A: a card saved for the $20 late-cancel or no-show fee; an advice call takes nothing. Flow B: nothing taken; a big job like a books cleanup takes a 25% retainer (the deposit) once its quote is OK'd.
pf.money.after: Flow A: the saved card charged when the CPA texts DONE, or the bill Rosie texts for an advice call. Flow B: the bill Rosie texts, or the firm's own monthly invoice for a monthly client.
pf.money.fees: Late-cancel or no-show fee: $20 ($40 for the books catch-up session), for a cancel less than 24 hours before, only after Sam says yes.
pf.money.how fees are set: Fixed or hourly. Never a share of a refund or of tax saved, and never set by what the return shows.
pf.money.first meeting credit: A paid first meeting is credited to the first year's fees if the client hires the firm.
pf.money.prices shown: A price shown stays good for 30 days after it was last shown, where the firm's rules or the state's rules require it.
pf.money.monthly plans: Their own yes on the secure page, cancel by one reply or link, a reminder every year, and a notice 30 days before a price change. A monthly fee with no visit, like monthly bookkeeping, is charged on the 1st to the saved card under the engagement letter's own yes: each charge is texted the day before, a declined card gets one pay link, and cancelling stops the next charge.
pf.money.tax: None by default; the rate comes from the state form where accounting work is taxed.
pf.money.rosfield: Pays Rosfield's $2 per confirmed booking, never more than $49 a person a month; a plan counts once a month. Switch: where the state's rules for CPAs bar or limit paying for referrals, the $2 is off for CPA work until Rosfield's lawyer confirms it (on the lawyer list).

pf.staff.who OKs what: Sam OKs every new client after the conflict check, and every price made for one client over his limit ($500 at Lee Accounting). Pat sees the same requests. Sam's answer wins.
pf.staff.stand-ins: Another CPA at the same firm, offered by name, and only if the client picks them. Nobody is moved to another CPA on silence: Sam calls instead. One exception: on a date that can't move, like a lender's deadline, Sam's default is a trusted stand-in CPA, and the client can still cancel with no fee.

pf.rules.engagement letter: Before any work beyond the first meeting: the scope, the fees and the client's document deadline, signed by both on the secure page, where the firm's rules or the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.no tax advice from Rosie: Rosie and the customer's AI never give tax or accounting advice. Questions wait for the CPA.
pf.rules.tax return information: Tax return information is used only to book and to pass to the firm. Rosie never uses it for anything else, under the firm's data-security agreement and where the federal rules for return information apply.
pf.rules.data-security agreement: The firm signs Rosie's data-security agreement before going live: how client files are kept, who opens them and how they're deleted.
pf.rules.deadlines: The filing deadline and any extension come from the client's engagement; Rosie never names a deadline of its own.
pf.rules.titles: The title 'CPA' only for licensed CPAs, as the business gives it (shown as given, not checked).
pf.rules.who may sign a return: A switch from the state's form.
pf.rules.referral fees: A switch from the state's form: where paying for a client sent to a CPA is barred or must be told to the client, the $2 follows that rule (on the lawyer list).
pf.rules.records: Booking records 7 years. Client files stay in the firm's own files, and uploads are kept or deleted as the firm sets in the portal.
pf.rules.right to cancel: Work sold at the client's home comes with a written right to cancel where the state's rules require it; a business's own premises usually don't.
pf.rules.status: Draft: finalized once the state forms are filled in.

matter most.thinking it over: No follow-up nudges; the quote holds 30 days.
matter most.a client who leaves: Their documents are handed back or deleted as the firm sets.

Pilot: from lawyer. A CPA firm runs like a consult: a first meeting with a named professional, a check before taking a client (here the owner's OK plus a conflict check), an engagement letter before the work, and documents only on the secure page. The lawyer's structure carried over (the conflict form on the secure page, the firm's own next steps after the meeting, privacy in texts). The lawyer's money choices were reversed, like the coach's: a CPA firm pays Rosfield's $2 and may take money before the work (a retainer on a big job), so the $2 splits take their yes branches and no deposit branch is turned off for that reason. The rename pairs were rebuilt from the master, so no lawyer words or pairs remain.
Cast: Sam Lee, CPA, owns Lee Accounting LLC (the master's main company, 750 Main St: bookkeeping, with payroll as its second kind of work; trade names Lee Bookkeeping and Lee Payroll) and Lee CPA Group PC (the master's second company, 220 Market St, Suite 4: CPA meetings at the office or by video). CPAs Nadia Shah and Felix Diaz (the master's Riley and Avery); Eli Price, staff accountant, and Milo Moore, bookkeeper (Jordan and Casey). Only licensed CPAs are called 'CPA'. Pat stays the office manager; Alex M. stays the customer and runs a bike store, Two Wheels Bikes, at 58 River Rd.
Flow A, the usual side: Alex names Nadia and books a 30-minute first meeting at the office, Sat Oct 24 at 11:00am (Lee CPA Group meets clients on Saturday mornings too; a video meeting is the A4-36 what-if). New client: the conflict form on the secure page (A4-43, A4-72), then Sam's OK, which is the master's A6-02 with Sam checking the names for a conflict and OKing a new client. A letter from the IRS or the state is read first by Felix (A6-16). Documents go on the secure page by Thu 6pm (own split A7-x01 to A7-x03; a missing item never moves the meeting). After the meeting: the engagement letter, the year's documents, the return's quote after the documents are seen, then monthly books and the yearly return (own steps A10-x01 to A10-x08, after A10-05 so the clock runs forward).
Flow B, the less usual side: Lee Accounting sends Eli to set up the books at Alex's store, Thu Oct 22 at 8:00am, before it opens. The engagement letter is the master's signed contract (B4-57 'Yes: a signed contract first', B4-61, B4-58, B4-59): Alex signs, then Sam checks the conflict form's names and signs, and his signature is his OK to take Alex on, so B6-03 books right away. The conflict form is B4-86. Visits read as set start times (B4-83 '2 A set start time'); the master's 8-10am window words are renamed to 8:00am.
Prices are the example firms' own, keeping the master's numbers so sums stay right. A: first meeting $35 (30 min, credited if hired), tax question meeting $40, extra document review $20, quick question call $25, tax planning meeting $55, books catch-up session $140 (2.5 hours, $40 fee), personal tax return priced from documents ($90 example), tax letter help priced at a meeting after a $25 review, advice call $35 a half hour. B: books setup visit $179, payroll setup visit $150, inventory count help $199, books cleanup priced from documents ($640, over Sam's $500 OK), records check priced at the visit, $89 trip fee (the master's service call), extra time $120 an hour. The engagement's own fees ($350 a month, a $600 business return) live only in the own steps A10-x02 to A10-x06.
Money paths. A: list|card|card (main: the first meeting, card saved for the $20 fee, charged at DONE; also the monthly books review plan), list|none|bill (the same meeting at a firm that saves no card, and advice calls billed by the half hour), photos|card|card (a flat fee per return quoted after the documents; the price label reads 'Priced from your documents first'). B: list|none|bill (main), list|none|own (a monthly client's visit or inventory count on the firm's own invoice), photos|deposit|bill (a retainer before a big job: the books cleanup). CPA firms don't hold money on cards, take full price before a meeting, or take payment at a front desk, so no other path is listed; A7-02's day-before hold branch is off. A free first meeting has no money path of its own (nothing before, nothing after).
Sign-up words (S1-13, S1-14, S1-16, S1-18, S1-38, S1-41, S1-42, S1-45, S1-46, S11-56, S11-58) are rewritten so Sam never sets a hold, a full price or a counter payment: Lee Accounting starts from nothing taken, with a 25% retainer on the books cleanup; Lee CPA Group saves a card for the $20 fee and charges it at DONE, with advice calls on the bill. The firm takes no payments at its front desk (it still checks people in there), which replaces the master's Saturday-morning no-front-desk story.
Rosfield's $2: a CPA firm pays it by default, since the no-$2 default covers human health practices and law firms only. The old flowchart's template said 'Referral fees: none: Rosfield pays none and takes none', and some states' rules for CPAs limit paying for referrals or require telling the client. So pf.money and pf.rules carry it as a switch from the state form, and it goes on the lawyer list.
Licenses: S1-60 takes 'No license: registration only' (bookkeeping and payroll); S1-63 takes the CPA firm's license or permit; S2-28 keeps both branches (splitsKept): CPAs are checked, the staff accountant and bookkeeper hold none and are never shown as 'CPA'. Who may sign a return is a switch from the state form (pf.license, pf.rules). S1-29 takes 'Yes: signed before going live': a data-security agreement, since the firm handles tax return information.
Privacy: tax ID numbers, bank details and income go only inside documents on the secure page; texts to Alex, Sam and the staff carry only names, the service and the time (A4-22, A4-23, A4-41, A6-02, A6-15, B4-24, B4-28, B6-14, A7-x01, A10-x04). A7-61's 'Someone has it' is off: nobody is moved to another CPA on silence, Sam calls.
Off beyond the plug-in splits: walk-ins, seats, spaces, drop-offs, stays, crews, minimums, damage holds, plans or insurance that pay, items held, rentals, aftercare, items not picked up, the master's proposal branch in A (the engagement letter is drawn on the main line), the day-before hold, a class roster, sent-now jobs, live lines, landlords, deliveries, outside checks, permits, parts, tips, pay over time, photo permission (B4-69), and B's weather, late part, first-step and form branches (the letter and the form are signed before the booking).

Not sure (for the reviewer): the master's low example prices for a CPA ($35 first meeting, a $90 personal return); Saturday meetings at a CPA firm (the master's date); the monthly bookkeeping fee charged to a card through Rosie (drawn in A10-x03 and A10-x06; a monthly fee with no visit is a gap); the engagement letter signed after the first meeting in A but before the visit in B; the firm 'takes no payments at its front desk' yet checks clients in there; the $2 and paying for referrals (lawyer list); A7-63's lender deadline as the date that can't move.
